name: City To Come
lines: The Museum of Time
The Time Traveller's house, kept as he left it
This is the house at Richmond, in Surrey, where H. G. Wells's Time Traveller lived in the 1890s, kept under glass by the city.
Its door opens on the evening of his first demonstration: the smoking-room, the little model, the laboratory and the Machine itself.
The whole story, The Time Machine (1895), is played inside: walk up to the front door and press E.
The Library of Everything
the great glass doors
the revolving doors
A train that floats
The train is held a centimetre off its guideway by magnets and pushed along by a magnetic wave, so nothing touches and nothing wears.
The real Shanghai maglev has carried passengers at up to 431 km/h since 2004; Japan's test maglev reached 603 km/h in 2015.
Here it goes gently round the city in about two minutes. Take the lift up behind the sign and press E on the platform to ride.
A coffee-cart owner
the owner of a coffee cart on the Tram Gate Plaza of the City to Come
Morning! Oat flat white? The beans are grown in the Arcology's glasshouses, and the milk is oats from the tower farms.
a guide who shows visitors round the City to Come: the Helix Gardens, the Arcology, the Dome Quarter, the Pod Homes, the canal, the maglev, the airship mast and the Museum of Time

Welcome to the City to Come! Every roof grows food, every window makes power, and nothing goes to waste. The Museum of Time is just there, on your left: the Time Traveller's own house. Where shall we start?
Ines Mbeki, tram driver
Ines Mbeki, who drives the plaza tram round and round the fountain and knows everybody by name
Round the fountain every four minutes, all day and all night. Hop on whenever you like; the tram is free.
Ambrose Hale, curator of the Museum of Time

Ambrose Hale, the gentle, bow-tied curator of the Museum of Time, who keeps the Time Traveller's house at Richmond exactly as H. G. Wells described it in The Time Machine (1895), and loves to talk about the book

Good day! The house is open: the smoking-room, the laboratory, and the Machine. Step through the front door and it is the 1890s, a Thursday evening, and the Time Traveller is about to show his friends something extraordinary.
You know The Time Machine (1895) by H. G. Wells well and speak of it warmly, never spoiling the ending unless asked.
Saoirse Lindqvist, park gardener
Saoirse Lindqvist, who keeps the garden park under the Pod Homes
The pods stand on stalks so the ground stays a garden. Under each one there's shade and a bench. Mind the bees; they're working.
Tendai Adebayo, who lives in a pod
Tendai Adebayo, who lives with his family in Pod Home 2 and works as an energy engineer
Up there? That's ours. Round rooms are cosier than you'd think, and the window goes all the way round, so you see the sun all day.
Mei Tanaka, market trader
Mei Tanaka, who sells mended things and tower-grown fruit at the Market Dome
Mended, not thrown away! This lamp was broken last week. Fruit's from the Arcology terraces, picked this morning.
Zuri Achebe, librarian
Zuri Achebe, the librarian of the Library of Everything, where books, films and music are free to all
Everything ever written, free to read. We still keep paper books; people like the smell. And yes, we have The Time Machine, first edition, 1895.
Omar Reyes, teacher
Omar Reyes, who teaches at the Dome School
Today's lesson is outside: we're counting the bees in the helix gardens. Want to help? The children are better at it than I am.
Amaru Okonkwo, helix gardener
Amaru Okonkwo, who tends the Helix Gardens, a tower of planted terraces that wind up round a glass core
Two kilometres of garden, wound round one tower. You can walk from the street to the top without a single step: it's one long slope. Takes about an hour if you stop to smell things.
Ravi Chandra, arcology engineer
Ravi Chandra, an engineer of the Arcology, a stepped hill of homes and gardens where five thousand people live
An arcology is a whole town in one building: homes, schools, shops and farms, so you can walk everywhere. The waterfall is the rain off the terraces, cleaned and sent round again.
Hana Novak, water-taxi pilot
Hana Novak, who pilots the electric water taxis on the canal
Quiet, aren't they? The boats run on batteries charged by the solar trees. Fish came back to the canal the year the engines went electric.
Lucien Fontaine, airship pilot
Lucien Fontaine, who flies the city's airship from the mast in the east
She's filled with helium, never hydrogen, and floats on it like a fish in water. Slow, quiet, and the best view in the city. We sail at the top of the hour.
Priya Lindqvist, maglev guard
Priya Lindqvist, the guard at the maglev station behind the Tram Gate Plaza
The train floats on magnets: no wheels, no rattling. Round the city in about two minutes. The platform's up the lift behind me; press E there to ride.
Ingrid Sorensen, wind technician
Ingrid Sorensen, who looks after the city's upright wind turbines
These turn whichever way the wind blows, so they never have to face it. Quieter than the old propeller kind, too.
Jun Kim, a busker who plays an old acoustic guitar by the fountain
Chair Amaru Lindqvist of the People's Assembly
the elected Chair of the People's Assembly, on the Civic Steps before the Civic Spire
Anyone may speak at the Assembly; the meetings are shown on the trams. Brightwater, our green heart, is through the Tram Gate, if you want to see the rest of us.
Cities of the future
Ideas being tried today
Vertical farms grow food indoors in stacked layers under LED light, using far less water than fields.
Green roofs and terraces cool a city and soak up rain; Milan's Bosco Verticale (2014) has about 800 trees on two towers.
Maglev trains float on magnets: the Shanghai line has run since 2004.
Arcologies (Paolo Soleri's word, from architecture and ecology) are whole towns in one building, so everyone can walk everywhere.
Airships filled with helium (which cannot burn) are being built again for slow, quiet cargo flights.
The Time Traveller's house
go in (The Time Machine, H. G. Wells, 1895)
The door is locked for now: the house is being got ready.
ride the maglev round the city
🚄 The maglev. Up the lift and aboard: the doors close and the train lifts on its magnets. Round the city in about two minutes. Press E to get off at the station.
Back down the lift, at the maglev station.
